hero.tagline: Manage your brand visibility in the AI era.

challenge.title: Challenge
challenge.subtitle: A new recommendation ecosystem
challenge.descriptionBefore: Traditional search engines are giving way to AI assistants. Your customers are increasingly seeking opinions and products within platforms like ChatGPT, Gemini, or Perplexity. If your brand is absent there, or if the AI provides incorrect or incomplete data,
challenge.descriptionAfter: you might not even be aware of.

solution.title: Solution by dentsu - LLM Brand Auditor
solution.description:
An AI system that evaluates a website's readiness for quoting and indexing by generative AI systems, while measuring and optimizing brand visibility in responses generated by popular AI chatbots.

Two modules. One complete picture of your AI visibility.

items.title: AI Readiness - Qualitative website audit.
items.description: We verify if your website is readable to the new generation of AI crawlers. Based on your URL, we identify specific changes in code and content to ensure your site becomes a reliable data source for AI assistants.

items.title: LLM Audit - Brand monitoring in AI chatbots.
items.description: We transform keywords into the questions real customers ask, then track how ChatGPT, Perplexity or Google AIO respond. You see your share of voice versus competitors, what AI says about your products, and which external sources - Reddit, YouTube, niche forums - are shaping those answers. We identify content gaps that need to be filled for your brand to dominate AI-generated answers.

items.title: AI Readiness Report.
items.description: Our system doesn't just report your absence in AI: it points out exactly which technical aspects to improve and what content to create to get you there.

items.title: Advantage in the new recommendation channel.
items.description: Secure a presence where the next generation of users - who are moving away from traditional search - make their purchasing decisions.

items.title: Full narrative control.
items.description: Gain insights into how often your brand appears compared to key competitors and understand exactly what AI models are saying about your products.

items.title: Time savings.
items.description: Weeks of manual prompting and screenshots become a single consolidated report - with prioritized changes a team can start implementing the same day.

items.title: Pre-campaign.
items.description: Before new communication goes live, understand how AI currently perceives your brand and what to shift first to make the campaign land.

items.title: Product launch.
items.description: Make sure new products are correctly indexed and recommended by AI assistants from day one, not six months after launch.

items.title: Crisis management.
items.description: Quickly detect AI hallucinations or negative narratives about your brand before they scale across every major chatbot.

items.title: Continuous optimization.
items.description: Track how AI responses evolve as you update your site content (AEO/GEO) - and keep the lead you just built.

items.title: Recommendations over raw data
items.description: Our system doesn't just report your absence in AI; it points out exactly what content needs to be created to appear there.

items.title: The dentsu ecosystem
items.description: Audit data is delivered directly to our media and creative teams, who can immediately implement content optimizations.

items.title: Enterprise-grade security
items.description: We guarantee full confidentiality and data isolation. Your resources are not used to train public AI models, and access is restricted to authorized users only.

items.question: My brand ranks well on Google. Why should I care about AI visibility?
items.answer: Google ranking and AI visibility are two separate things. When someone asks ChatGPT, Perplexity, or Gemini for a product recommendation, the answer doesn't come from your Google position - it comes from what these models have learned about your brand from various sources across the web. A brand that dominates traditional search can be completely absent from AI-generated responses. LLM Brand Auditor measures exactly that gap and tells you what to do about it.

items.question: What exactly does LLM Brand Auditor check and what do I get at the end?
items.answer: The product works in two modules. The first - AI Readiness - audits your website to check whether it's structured in a way that AI crawlers can read, index, and cite. The second - LLM Audit - transforms your keywords into real user questions and tracks how ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Perplexity, and Google AIO respond: how often your brand appears, what they say about it, and where the gaps are. You receive a consolidated report with a prioritized list of technical and content changes - ready to brief your team the same day.

items.question: Can AI really say something wrong about my brand and how would I even know?
items.answer: Yes. This is one of the most underestimated risks in AI-era marketing. AI models can generate incorrect, outdated, or misleading information about your brand, products, or pricing - a phenomenon known as hallucination. Without systematic monitoring, these errors spread silently across every major chatbot, shaping purchasing decisions before you're even aware of the problem. LLM Brand Auditor detects these narratives early, so you can act before they scale.

items.question: Is this a platform I log into, or a service delivered by your team?
items.answer: It's a managed service. You don't log in and figure it out alone. Our specialists configure the audit to your brand, category, and competitors and run the analysis. You get conclusions ready to act on, not a dashboard to manage.

items.question: How is my data protected during the audit?
items.answer: Full confidentiality and data isolation by design. Your briefs, keywords, and analysis results are never used to train public AI models. Every engagement runs in a dedicated environment with access limited to named users only. Our setup is built to clear legal and security reviews without complications - so you can proceed with confidence, not with caveats.

metadata.title: Echo | dentsu AI Stack
metadata.description: Advanced sentiment and consumer opinion analytics.

hero.tagline: Advanced sentiment and consumer opinion analytics.

challenge.title: Challenge
challenge.subtitle: Information noise and source fragmentation.
challenge.descriptionAfter: where the primary issue is not a lack of data, but the difficulty of extracting meaningful insights from a sea of irrelevant mentions. Brands often base their decisions on incomplete or misinterpreted data, leading to costly mistakes in product and communication strategies.

solution.title: Solution by dentsu - Echo
solution.description: An AI system that analyzes thousands of digital conversations surrounding your brand and products with extreme precision. You will discover not only what consumers are saying, but also why - from specific product features to service quality. Echo operates at scale, transforming scattered comments into actionable insights that help you better align your offering with real customer needs.

items.title: Understanding real needs.
items.description: No more guesswork. Echo provides the hard data necessary to build strategies based on the authentic motivations, needs, and pain points of your consumers.

items.title: Aspect-based analytics.
items.description: Move from general sentiment scores to granular aspect analysis. This allows for precise identification of how specific product features, services, or brand image elements are perceived.

items.title: AI Summarization.
items.description: Automatic generation of concise summaries for thousands of posts and reviews, allowing for the quick identification of key trends.

items.title: Time savings.
items.description: Echo significantly shortens the time from data collection to key insight generation.

items.title: Brand health monitoring.
items.description: Systematically track consumer opinion trends over the long term - and stay ahead of shifts instead of reacting to them.

items.title: Competitor analysis.
items.description: Compare how specific features of your products are perceived versus competitors.

items.title: Pre-campaign audit.
items.description: Map the opinion landscape for your brand and your competitors - identify the real barriers to purchase and real drivers of preference.

items.title: Post-launch reception.
items.description: Get a detailed picture of how your new product landed - from early users, in their own words, across every platform they post on.

items.question: What data does Echo analyze, and where does it come from?
items.answer: Echo tracks brand mentions across social media, news portals, forums, and review sites. Data enters the system through platform APIs, and is cleaned and normalized before reaching the analytics engine.

items.question: Can Echo handle tens of thousands of mentions at once?
items.answer: Yes - Echo processes data in a streaming, distributed architecture, so high volume doesn't slow the system down. When mentions spike during a product launch or PR crisis, reporting doesn't lag and no mention is missed.

items.question: Does Echo detect sarcasm, irony, or negativity disguised as a positive tone?
items.answer: Yes - Echo analyses the full context of a statement: tone, punctuation, and the contrast between the content and other users' reactions. This lets it recognize "great, another outage" as a negative mention, not praise - without this, growing customer dissatisfaction could go unnoticed. When classification confidence is low, the system flags the mention for manual review.

items.question: Why a 5-level sentiment scale, when the market usually settles for 3?
items.answer: A positive/neutral/negative scale confuses minor dissatisfaction with a genuine reputational crisis. Echo's five levels let you immediately see which mention needs an urgent response and which can wait. The result: sharper alerts and better allocation of your team's resources.

items.question: When is the best time to use Echo?
items.answer: Echo works well in both modes - as a tool for continuous brand health monitoring, and as a one-off, in-depth analysis before a key moment like a product launch or campaign kickoff. A one-time audit is usually a good starting point, with a move to ongoing monitoring as a natural next step, so you don't lose sight of changes over time.

metadata.title: Context Hub | dentsu AI Stack
metadata.description: AI-Powered Knowledge Base and Virtual Assistant

hero.tagline: Your AI-powered knowledge base and Virtual Assistant.

challenge.title: Challenge
challenge.subtitle: Fragmented knowledge, lost efficiency, overloaded teams.
challenge.descriptionBefore: The bigger the organisation, the more scattered its knowledge - projects, HR procedures, legal documents, and case studies get lost across dozens of systems and databases. Teams waste time searching for information and answering the same questions repeatedly, instead of focusing on work that moves the business forward.

solution.title: Solution by dentsu - Context Hub
solution.description: Context Hub indexes and surfaces all organisation's critical data - from project descriptions, through HR procedures, to legal documentation - in one consistent source of truth. Just ask: the Virtual Assistant understands questions in natural language, searches your data - including visual content through multimodal analysis - and responds instantly, the way a knowledgeable colleague would, not a file search engine.

items.title: Fast, verified answers.
items.description: Get information instantly through an intuitive chatbot interface, eliminating the need to search multiple sources or wait for a colleague's response.

items.title: Better decision-making.
items.description: Instant access to information instead of digging through multiple sources or waiting on a colleague - with the certainty that the answer is consistent and verified, no matter who's asking.

items.title: Lighter workload for teams.
items.description: Routine questions are handled by Context Hub, not people - freeing HR, legal, and project teams to focus on work that requires their expertise.

items.title: Centralised knowledge.
items.description: A single repository that grows with the organisation and protects its knowledge - even as people leave.

items.title: Project management.
items.description: Fast access to historical case studies and project documentation, e.g. "show me projects using augmented reality".

items.title: Onboarding and Training.
items.description: New employees ask about procedures and company policy instead of digging through papers, e.g. "how do I submit a vacation request?".

items.title: Legal and compliance support.
items.description: Instant access to regulations, contracts, and current standards, e.g. "what's the latest version of our GDPR policy?" - reducing legal risk.

items.title: Developing new strategies and offers.
items.description: A knowledge base and source of inspiration for new solutions, instead of starting every project from scratch.

items.question: Is Context Hub just a file search tool, or something more?
items.answer: Much more - a search tool only returns a list of documents, leaving the user to search through their content manually. Context Hub works as an intelligent knowledge assistant: it understands questions asked in natural language, instantly analyses the relevant documents in context, and generates a precise, ready-to-use answer with links to specific sources - exactly as a dedicated expert would.

items.question: What types of documents and systems can Context Hub integrate and analyse?
items.answer: Context Hub indexes project descriptions, internal procedures (e.g. HR, operational), legal documentation, spreadsheets, and multimedia files, among others. This means it can easily connect, for example, information in a contract's text with data from a financial table.

items.question: Will every employee have access to all data, or can visibility be restricted - for example, for HR or legal documents?
items.answer: Context Hub doesn't change your existing security policy - it operates strictly within it. Access to documents is configured according to your organisation's structure and each user's existing permissions. This means sensitive files - such as legal contracts or HR data - will only be visible to and analysed by the assistant for employees who already had direct access to them.

items.question: What happens when Context Hub doesn't know the answer to a question? Is there a risk it will "make up" information?
items.answer: Context Hub eliminates the risk of "hallucinating" facts - every answer is grounded in verified company documents, with a link to the source. If the knowledge base lacks the information needed, the assistant says so directly, instead of guessing.

items.question: Does Context Hub support documents and queries in different languages?
items.answer: Context Hub translates and processes knowledge dynamically, on the fly. This means an international team can ask a question in Polish, English, or German, and the assistant will find the relevant information in source documents written in a completely different language, and generate the answer in the language of the question.

metadata.title: Sniffer | dentsu AI Stack
metadata.description: Be the first to know what your competitors - and the web around your brand - are doing.

hero.tagline: Be the first to know what your competitors - and the web around your brand - are doing.

challenge.title: Challenge
challenge.subtitle: Real-time competition.
challenge.descriptionBefore: Competitors change prices, offers, and messaging every day - and you find out too late, or by accident. Manually checking dozens of pages isn't feasible, standard alerts drown in noise, and "HTML change detected" doesn't tell you what happened.
challenge.descriptionAfter: and market moves you don't even know exist.

solution.title: Solution by dentsu - Sniffer
solution.description:
An AI system that continuously monitors your competitors' and market's websites, detects changes (prices, offers, products, messaging), understands their business significance, and turns a raw stream of changes into a ready-to-use briefing.

Two modules. One complete picture of what's happening around your brand.

items.title: Change Tracker - monitoring changes on websites.
items.description: You specify which pages to watch - yours and your competitors'. Sniffer monitors them continuously, detects changes, and - instead of showing a raw record - explains what changed and why it matters. Every change is added to that brand's timeline.

items.title: Scout - spotting opportunities and competitors.
items.description: You define what you're looking for — competitors, offers, opportunities. Scout continuously scans the web and surfaces only what's genuinely new — no repeats, nothing you already know.

items.title: Early signal on competitor moves.
items.description: You're the first to know when a competitor changes a price, launches a product, or reworks their messaging - before the market catches on.

items.title: Full control over what you watch.
items.description: You decide which brands, pages, and topics to track - and in return, you get a ready-made synthesis, not a list of raw changes to analyse.

items.title: Meaning instead of noise.
items.description: Sniffer doesn't just say "the page changed" - AI analysis explains what changed and why it matters, with a link to the source.

items.title: Time saved.
items.description: Instead of hours spent checking dozens of pages, you get one organized stream of changes - so you immediately know what to read first.

items.title: Competitor monitoring.
items.description: Prices, promotions, new products, changes in messaging.

items.title: Before a campaign.
items.description: Check what the market is doing before you launch.

items.title: Risk management.
items.description: Quickly catch changes to terms, statuses, outages, or negative signals.

items.title: Continuous observation.
items.description: Keep an up-to-date timeline of changes for key assets and brands.

items.question: What's the difference between the Change Tracker and Scout modules - and do I need both?
items.answer: Change Tracker monitors specific pages you've selected and alerts you when something changes. Scout works more broadly: you enter any query - it could be any business challenge you want to keep an eye on - and Scout scans the entire web, notifying you when something new appears. Together, they give you the full picture - what you're watching directly, and what you didn't yet know you should be watching.

items.question: Does Sniffer distinguish real changes (e.g. a new offer) from cosmetic ones (e.g. a rotating banner, a footer date)?
items.answer: Yes - Sniffer doesn't compare page code, it analyses content, so it recognises the difference between a change with real business significance and visual noise. Cookie banners, rotating hero elements, or auto-updating footer dates don't trigger false alerts.

items.question: How often does Sniffer check monitored pages - will a change be detected within hours, or days?
items.answer: Frequency is configurable - from checks every minute, to several times a day, to once a week - and you adjust it to the importance of each asset: more often for key competitors' pages, less often for peripheral monitoring.

items.question: In what format, and how often, do I receive a summary of changes?
items.answer: Changes are added to that brand's timeline in real time, and you also receive an email briefing with the most important items prioritised for you. You don't need to review the raw stream of changes yourself - you get a ready-made synthesis.

items.question: Is monitoring competitors' websites this way compliant with the law and those websites' terms of service?
items.answer: Sniffer only analyses publicly available content - the same content any visitor to the page can see. It doesn't bypass security measures, log into accounts, or access data that isn't publicly available.
